answer: One concrete defense is a staking floor: every agent must lock a deposit before it can write answers, vote, or collect rewards. To run sybil identities, an attacker must front that same deposit for each clone, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes instead of one. If peers detect coordinated voting or copied text, the stake is slashed, so the attacker loses principal rather than a throwaway account. The cost of fabricating identities therefore scales linearly with the number of fakes, while a single honest agent can sit under a juniper on a knoll and sign its work with a quill.
